South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 77 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 10/14/25 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent lower extremity edema, and ongoing fatigue assessment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit concerning his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and generalized fatigue. He reports that over the past month, his respiratory symptoms have not significantly improved, with continued nocturnal wheezing episodes. He has been adhering to his medication regimen, including the increased dosage of fluticasone/salmeterol, yet he still experiences increased shortness of breath during exertion and occasional episodes of orthopnea.
The patient expresses frustration regarding the persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, which remains at 1+ pitting despite dietary sodium restriction and leg elevation. He notes that the swelling is more pronounced by the end of the day and affects his mobility. He denies any pain, redness, or warmth in the affected areas but expresses concern about potential worsening.
Mr. Fairfax's fatigue persists, described as an overwhelming sense of tiredness that is not alleviated by rest. He reports that his ability to participate in daily activities has diminished, and he feels less inclined to engage in social activities. He has not experienced any recent weight changes, but he does report sleeping poorly due to discomfort from his edema.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, - dyspnea on exertion, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, increased use to twice daily 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily (increased dosage) 4. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain 5. Furosemide 60 mg daily
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 82, BP 130/80, RR 22, O2 sat 91% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and slightly anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.5, Hgb 12.7, Hct 37.5, Plt 218 2. BMP: Na 136, K 4.2, Cl 96, CO2 24, BUN 19, Cr 1.3, Glucose 88 3. BNP: 450 (slightly elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Given the persistent nocturnal wheezing and exertional dyspnea, consider adding a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) to his regimen. Reassess inhaler technique and medication adherence. Schedule follow-up in 1 month. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists despite current management. Consider increasing furosemide to 80 mg daily and refer to a nephrologist for further evaluation. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage Mr. Fairfax to elevate his legs regularly. 4. Fatigue: Given the stable thyroid function tests and no signs of anemia, consider a referral to physical therapy for deconditioning and to enhance activity tolerance. Schedule follow-up CBC and metabolic panel in one month to monitor for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
